001package io.github.ai4ci.config.inhost;
002
003import org.immutables.value.Value;
004
005import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeInfo;
006import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeName;
007import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonDeserialize;
008import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonSerialize;
009
010import io.github.ai4ci.abm.inhost.InHostStochasticState;
011import io.github.ai4ci.flow.builders.DefaultInHostStochasticStateInitialiser;
012import io.github.ai4ci.functions.Distribution;
013import io.github.ai4ci.functions.SimpleDistribution;
014import io.github.ai4ci.util.Sampler;
015
016/**
017 * Parameters for a stochastic in‑host viral dynamics model.
018 *
019 * <p>
020 * This interface defines the numerical inputs and distributions used to
021 * initialise the discrete stochastic in‑host model implemented by
022 * {@link InHostStochasticState}. Values here are sampled by the default
023 * initialiser {@link DefaultInHostStochasticStateInitialiser} to construct an
024 * initial {@code InHostStochasticState} for each infected individual. The
025 * parameters control initial pool sizes, immune capacity and activation
026 * dynamics, rates of viral replication and infection, and the calibration
027 * cutoff for what constitutes a disease‑level viral load.
028 *
029 * <p>
030 * Keep descriptions concise: the initialiser samples distributional entries
031 * (see methods returning {@link Distribution}) and copies scalar parameters
032 * directly into the initial in‑host state. Downstream updates are performed by
033 * {@link InHostStochasticState#update(Sampler,double,double)} which uses these
034 * initial values to govern stochastic transitions.
035 *
036 * @author Rob Challen
037 */
038@Value.Immutable
039@JsonSerialize(as = ImmutableStochasticModel.class)
040@JsonDeserialize(as = ImmutableStochasticModel.class)
041@JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME)
042@JsonTypeName("stochastic")
043public interface StochasticModel extends InHostConfiguration {
044
045        /**
046         * A sensible default configuration for the stochastic in‑host model.
047         *
048         * <p>
049         * This instance provides default distributions and scalars used in examples
050         * and tests. The {@link DefaultInHostStochasticStateInitialiser} will sample
051         * the distributional entries from this object when creating a fresh
052         * {@link InHostStochasticState}.
053         */
054        ImmutableStochasticModel DEFAULT = ImmutableStochasticModel.builder()
055                .setDescription(
056                        "A complex in host model with a target cell model with immunity, and virion components"
057                )
058                .setTargetCellCount(10000)
059                .setImmuneTargetRatio(SimpleDistribution.logNorm(1D, 0.1))
060                .setImmuneActivationRate(SimpleDistribution.logNorm(1D, 0.1))
061                .setImmuneWaningRate(SimpleDistribution.logNorm(1D / 150, 0.01))
062                .setInfectionCarrierProbability(SimpleDistribution.point(0D))
063                .setTargetRecoveryRate(SimpleDistribution.logNorm(1D / 7, 0.1))
064                .setBaselineViralInfectionRate(1D)
065                .setBaselineViralReplicationRate(4D)
066                .setVirionsDiseaseCutoff(1000)
067                // .setTargetSymptomsCutoff( 0.2 )
068                .build();
069
070        /**
071         * Baseline per‑virion infection rate used to calibrate the infection
072         * probability.
073         *
074         * <p>
075         * The scalar is copied into the initial in‑host state. It is converted into
076         * a per‑time‑step probability during updates and therefore directly affects
077         * how readily virions convert susceptible targets into exposed cells in
078         * {@link InHostStochasticState#update(Sampler, double, double)}.
079         *
080         * @return baseline viral infection rate (scalar)
081         */
082        Double getBaselineViralInfectionRate();
083
084        /**
085         * Baseline viral replication rate used to determine virion production.
086         *
087         * <p>
088         * This scalar sets the expected production per infected cell and is
089         * sampled/copied by the initialiser into the host state. Larger values
090         * increase the expected Poisson rate of new virions produced each step,
091         * driving faster viral load growth.
092         *
093         * @return baseline viral replication rate (scalar)
094         */
095        Double getBaselineViralReplicationRate();
096
097        /**
098         * Distribution for the immune activation (priming) rate.
099         *
100         * <p>
101         * This distribution is sampled by the initialiser to set the host's
102         * propensity to prime immune cells in response to exposed or infected
103         * targets. A higher sampled value leads to faster priming and earlier immune
104         * activity during {@code InHostStochasticState.update}.
105         *
106         * @return a distribution for immune priming rates
107         */
108        Distribution getImmuneActivationRate();
109
110        /**
111         * Distribution for the immune to target cell ratio.
112         *
113         * <p>
114         * The initialiser samples this distribution to set the starting total immune
115         * count via floor(targets * ratio). This controls immune capacity relative
116         * to target cells and influences neutralisation and clearance probabilities
117         * in subsequent stochastic updates.
118         *
119         * @return a distribution producing immune:target ratios used at
120         *         initialisation
121         */
122        Distribution getImmuneTargetRatio();
123
124        /**
125         * Distribution for the waning rate of active immune cells.
126         *
127         * <p>
128         * The initialiser samples this entry to determine how quickly active
129         * effectors transition to senescent states. Faster waning reduces long‑ term
130         * immune activity and can increase susceptibility to reinfection in the
131         * simulation.
132         *
133         * @return a distribution for immune waning rates
134         */
135        Distribution getImmuneWaningRate();
136
137        /**
138         * Distribution giving the probability an exposed cell becomes a chronic
139         * carrier.
140         *
141         * <p>
142         * Sampled at initialisation, this controls the per‑cell probability that an
143         * exposed target will evade clearance and enter a persistent reservoir. Even
144         * if the default is zero, non‑zero values alter long‑term infection dynamics
145         * and the pool of targets available for future replication.
146         *
147         * @return a distribution for chronic infection carrier probability
148         */
149        Distribution getInfectionCarrierProbability();
150
151        /**
152         * Total number of target cells modelled for a single host.
153         *
154         * <p>
155         * The initialiser places this value into the created
156         * {@link InHostStochasticState} as both the total target pool and the
157         * initial susceptible pool. It therefore sets the scale of the infection:
158         * larger pools reduce per‑cell exposure for a given number of virions and
159         * change the saturation behaviour in the coverage calculations used during
160         * infection updates.
161         *
162         * @return the initial total target cell count
163         */
164        Integer getTargetCellCount();
165
166        /**
167         * Distribution for the target cell recovery (regeneration) rate.
168         *
169         * <p>
170         * The initialiser samples this distribution to set the baseline rate at
171         * which removed or damaged targets are replaced. Higher recovery rates
172         * replenish susceptible targets more quickly and can shorten the period of
173         * high severity in the in‑host simulation.
174         *
175         * @return a distribution for target recovery rates used at initialisation
176         */
177        Distribution getTargetRecoveryRate();
178
179        /**
180         * Calibration parameter defining the unit of virions considered
181         * disease‑level.
182         *
183         * <p>
184         * The initialiser stores this cutoff on the host state; it is used to
185         * normalise virion counts into a unitless viral load proxy and to scale
186         * external virion doses. Changing this value moves the threshold for when an
187         * individual's viral load is treated as clinically relevant in the
188         * simulation.
189         *
190         * @return the virion disease cutoff used for normalisation and dosing
191         */
192        Integer getVirionsDiseaseCutoff();
193
194}
